messages:
alex (partnerships): quick heads-up: OpenModelX reached out about adding their LLM to our catalog. they want Hosted + Dedicated + Private distribution. can we huddle on what approvals we need? :wave:

maria (legal): first ask  do we have the exact license text? many models tag themselves 'open' but restrict commercial or redistribution. we need to confirm redistribution/grant language.

alex (partnerships): they linked their repo; license header says 'OpenModelX License v1.0 (permissive)' but the body is thin on redistribution details. they want us to list and potentially do joint announce.

cj (eng-ml): technical checklist: artifact formats (HF repo? safetensors? torchscript?), availability of quantized weights, permission to modify/quantize/optimize, and any export control notes. if license forbids modifications we can't apply our kernel optimizations.

maria (legal): priority checklist: 1) explicit distribution grant for Hosted/Dedicated/Private 2) permission to sublicense to customers 3) permission for modification (incl. quantization/optimization) 4) export control/EAR statement 5) IP/patent indemnity scope and liability cap 6) permission for security & safety scans.

samir (product): GTM items: logo & trademark use, announcement embargo windows, co-marketing rights, marketplace listing fees or revenue share expectations. if they expect rev share that affects marketplace economics.

ellie (gtm): also: cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure) have packaging requirements for images/containers. if they want a Marketplace-AMI/container for Dedicated/Private we need their artifacts and marketplace contract. partners-bot, drop the intake form link?

partners-bot: vendor intake (model provider)  https://rwd.partners/internal/vendor-intake  attach license + artifact manifest + contact POC.

alex (partnerships): proposed owners: maria reviews license & drafts distribution grant; cj validates artifact/ops constraints; ellie/samir handle marketplace & co-marketing checklist; alex collects responses + SLA/support matrix. target: draft term sheet by end of week. good?

maria (legal): i'll draft a minimal distribution grant. prelim snippet: 

```
Model Distribution Grant: Licensor hereby grants Redwood Inference, its affiliates, and customers a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free right to host, reproduce, distribute, modify (including quantization and optimization), sublicense, and otherwise make available the Model and Model Weights as part of Redwood's hosted services, dedicated deployments, and customer-managed private deployments, subject to export control laws and Licensor's attribution requirements.
```

maria (legal): also need to request a limited IP indemnity in case of third-party claims and a liability cap tied to fees. will share redline.

cj (eng-ml): add explicit permission to run static security/safety scans and to deploy mitigations (filters, stop-sequences). we should be allowed to ship updated model wrappers to address safety issues.

maria (legal): will add clause: "Permission to perform security and safety analysis and to deploy mitigations, including but not limited to prompt filters, response guards, and weight modifications for safety patches."

samir (product): timeline: if they accept, can we do a private/internal listing for perf testing in ~2 weeks and a public marketplace listing in ~6 weeks? need ~4 weeks for marketing + security review.

ellie (gtm): 6 weeks sounds fine. request POC for co-marketing, logo assets, trademark consent, case study permission, and whether there is any embargo for announcements.

alex (partnerships): i'll request: license text, artifact URIs, confirmation on quantization/optimization rights, support/SLA matrix (CVEs, critical fixes), co-marketing permissions, trademark/logo usage, export control statement, performance profile/sample prompts. will paste answers here.

partners-bot: note: attach NDA/LOI on vendor intake if required by upstream legal.

cj (eng-ml): dev note: ask them for performance baselines (latency @ 8k context, QPS, memory footprint) so we can estimate cost per token on our runtime and impact of quantization.

maria (legal): red flag: if license contains 'non-commercial' or dual-license clauses requiring paid commercial terms, we must get the commercial license terms. do not onboard until commercial rights are explicit.

samir (product): edge case: BYOL (bring-your-own-license) for Private deployments reduces redistribution risk. do we want to offer BYOL if the license is restrictive?

cj (eng-ml): we already support BYOL for Private but Dedicated/Hosted need redistribution grants. BYOL still needs patching rights and permission to run mitigations.

alex (partnerships): plan: push for permissive distribution grant. offer BYOL Private-only fallback if they won't permit Hosted/Dedicated redistribution. i'll update when they reply. thanks all. :v:
